title: Loops
summary: Rust has three looping keywords: while, loop, and for.
lecture: Rust has three looping keywords, and they work much like their equivalents in other languages. `while` repeats as long as its condition is true. `for` walks over anything iterable, most often a range like `1..5` or a collection. `loop` repeats forever until something breaks out of it.

`break` leaves the loop and `continue` skips to the next turn. One thing is different from most languages. A `break` inside `loop` can carry a value out, and that value becomes the result of the loop. This makes `loop` the natural choice when you are searching for something.

A `for` loop over a collection borrows it by default when you write `for x in &items`. Writing `for x in items` consumes the collection instead. The ownership decks explain why, so for now prefer the borrowing form.

example.caption: while tests a condition, for walks a range.
